concepts.name: Store shock - gasp, hand to mouth, drink drops, point
concepts.what: Walking down a store aisle, the person spots something off-screen, freezes, gasps with hand over mouth, drops the drink/basket or points and lunges (often held back by a partner).
concepts.why: A human face in shock is the strongest stop signal on the feed; the cause is withheld (curiosity gap) and the shop setting reads as accidental footage + scarcity (FOMO).
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2-3 s medium/side shot of the gasp + drink drop + point (P04 / V080 / N001 style). Recast character + Christmas-dressed generic aisle as the start image; the product stays OFF-screen, whip-pan to the shelf is a separate cut.

concepts.name: Walks up and grabs it off the store shelf
concepts.what: A shopper (or POV hand) reaches to a shelf/pallet, takes the boxed product and drops it into the cart/basket - calm, no big reaction.
concepts.why: Quiet social proof: someone like me is buying it right now. The most repeatable store opener and the least ad-like.
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2-3 s POV or over-the-shoulder reach-grab-drop into cart (P03 / P07 / V050). Start image = generic shelf wall stocked with our unbranded box.

concepts.name: Store stampede / crowd rush at the pallet
concepts.what: Several shoppers converge on one pallet and grab boxes frantically, or a long queue holding the same box.
concepts.why: Herd behaviour = instant social proof and scarcity; the viewer's brain asks 'what are they all grabbing?'.
concepts.genjutsu: Hard for single-character motion control. Use Seedance from a start plate of a warehouse aisle with a stacked pallet (3-4 s); optionally Genjutsu one hero shopper running out with the box.

concepts.name: Pulls a cloth/sheet/towel off to reveal
concepts.what: The product (or a display) sits under a cloth, sheet, towel or blanket; hands or staff whip/peel it off in one move.
concepts.why: Open loop from frame 1 (what is under it?) closed within 2-3 s; the whip gives motion energy, a counted '3-2-1' adds a built-in timer.
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2-3 s cloth-pull (P08 two staff / P09 bed / V111 POV hand). Start image with the covered shape; the cloth physics come from the driving clip.

concepts.name: Holds it up and lets it drop / fling open
concepts.what: A rolled or folded garment/blanket is held overhead or at arm's length, then released or flung so it unfurls to full length in one motion.
concepts.why: A shape-change (small roll -> huge full-length object) is a visual surprise the eye must follow; shows size and design in 2 s.
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2-3 s front-on, full body, static camera, arms up holding the roll then the drop (N004 / N002 / N008). Character + room start image + product refs; best fit of all concepts.

concepts.name: Pulls hood/mask/eye-cover over the face in one move
concepts.what: Hands go to the hood (or mask, sleep cover), pull it up and over the head, often zipping it up to the eyes.
concepts.why: A face disappearing is a pattern interrupt; the silhouette change is satisfying and the 'anti-social' identity is instantly readable.
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2-3 s waist-up, static camera, pull-hood-up (+zip) in one take (V001 / V100 / N021). Night parking lot or park start image.

concepts.name: Throws/swings it on over the head in one motion
concepts.what: The garment is swung around the shoulders or pulled down over the head in one fluid move (hoodie, poncho, posture bra, car cover over a car).
concepts.why: The instant from 'not wearing' to 'wearing' is a micro-transformation; one continuous body move holds the eye.
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2-3 s full-body or waist-up put-on (V061 plane aisle / N009 cape swing / V115). Static camera, product refs for the garment.

concepts.name: Unbag / cut / lift the lid - opens the package
concepts.what: POV or close hands rip a plastic bag, cut a paper bag with scissors, slide off a wrap, or lift a lid and pull the product out.
concepts.why: Unboxing tension (what is inside?) plus tactile ASMR (rip, cut, peel); POV hands put the viewer in the buyer's seat.
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2-3 s POV hands tearing/cutting the bag on the lap (V064 chairlift / V088 scissors). Works with Genjutsu when hands are the only actor; for small objects Seedance from a start plate is often cleaner.

concepts.name: Someone hands/drops the gift on you - POV
concepts.what: First-person on a couch/bed: a partner/mom tosses or hands a wrapped box onto your lap (or the gift lies at your feet), and you look down at it.
concepts.why: POV makes the viewer the receiver; 'hard to gift' tension resolved in-frame triggers the gifting impulse.
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2-3 s POV from the lap, giver walks in and drops the box (P10 / V072 / V103). Genjutsu on the giver; legs in frame from the start image.

concepts.name: Holds/thrusts it up to the camera
concepts.what: The person holds the product (or its box/bag) up to the lens, shoves it toward the camera, or turns it around to show it.
concepts.why: Direct address: the object fills the frame and gets close to the viewer; simple, but it relies on the product looking odd/novel at first glance.
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2 s arm thrust toward lens or two-hand hold-up (V031 / N039). Easy Genjutsu; product refs carry the look.

concepts.name: Strangers react / laugh at it in public
concepts.what: The wearer/user stands deadpan in a public place (elevator, police stop, plane, club line) while a stranger bursts out laughing or stares.
concepts.why: Social proof via reactions: the viewer laughs with the stranger; the deadpan contrast + public stakes make it shareable.
concepts.genjutsu: Two people: drive the reacting stranger with a 2-3 s laughing-reaction clip (N005 elevator) and keep the wearer static in the start image; or Seedance from a start plate.

concepts.name: Slapstick fail - falls off the ladder, things crash, fire
concepts.what: Someone attempting decor/DIY falls off a ladder, the decor falls on them, they slip, or the lights catch fire - one unbroken take.
concepts.why: Physical comedy + schadenfreude stops the scroll; it is also the 'problem' that the product solves, so the payoff feels earned.
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2-4 s fall from ladder/step stool (P11 / P12) or slip; Genjutsu copies the body physics. Fire/smoke and props falling are safer with Seedance.

concepts.name: Struggles with the old way / acts out the problem
concepts.what: Frustrated person wrestles tangled lights, an inflatable, cotton snow, a paper stencil, a DIY hack, or acts out the pain (cold, sick, swollen) before the 'Vs...' cut.
concepts.why: Relatable pain makes the viewer nod ('that's me'); the exaggerated frustration sets up the before/after contrast.
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2-3 s of the frustrated wrestling motion (V084 tangled lights / V120 inflatable Santa). Static camera, full body; the 'Vs...' product shot is a separate clip.

concepts.name: Satisfying close-up demo - press, click, snap, light up
concepts.what: Tight close-up of the product working: press, click, snap, squeeze, pour water, plug in - the mechanism does something visible.
concepts.why: ASMR / mechanical satisfaction and an immediate 'how does that work?'; no context needed to understand the motion.
concepts.genjutsu: Mostly object physics -> Seedance from a close-up start plate (3 s). Genjutsu only when hands drive the action (press/squeeze), with a 2-3 s hand clip.

concepts.name: Flops / sinks / wraps into it on bed or sofa
concepts.what: The person crawls, jumps or sits into the bed/pillow/chair and sinks in, or is already buried under it and peeks out.
concepts.why: Embodied comfort - the viewer feels the softness; calm, slow-burn opener that suits cozy products and night scrolling.
concepts.genjutsu: Driving clip: 2-3 s flop/crawl into bed or sit into chair (N016 / V097 / V046); static wide or top-down camera.

concepts.name: Absurd object / something pops out
concepts.what: An impossible image: a pet pops out of a hoodie hole, a pillow comes out of the oven, a giant cap flies into frame, a 'puppy' turns out to be a bag.
concepts.why: Pure pattern interrupt - the brain cannot classify the image and must keep watching to resolve it.
concepts.genjutsu: Animals and impossible objects -> Seedance from a start plate (3 s); Genjutsu only for the human part (e.g. officer reaction).

clip.label: Clip prompt — the one in the cut
clip.text:
AUDIO RULE - HIGHEST PRIORITY, READ THIS FIRST: this clip has NO MUSIC OF ANY KIND. No background song, no soundtrack, no score, no melody, no instruments, no singing, no humming, no jingle, no Christmas song, no festive music bed, no ambient musical pad, no strings, no piano, no bells used as music. The audio track contains ONLY real natural sound recorded in that room plus the spoken line. The attached reference video is SILENT and has no audio track at all - take nothing from it but movement. If any music appears anywhere in the 4 seconds the clip is wrong.

TASK: image-to-video. The start image is frame 0.0s. Hold its wardrobe, store, lighting and lens exactly.

[1] SUMMARY
A woman in a supermarket Christmas aisle stops her trolley, reacts in shock and points off-camera; the camera whip-pans right onto a pallet of dark-green product boxes. Handheld vertical UGC. 4 seconds, one continuous take with one whip pan.

[2] GLOBAL STYLE
Real handheld phone footage filmed by a friend walking behind her. Natural retail lighting warmed by the red and gold decorations. Extremely sharp, clean, well exposed. Subtle handheld breathing throughout. The ONLY blur in the clip is the deliberate horizontal motion blur inside the whip pan. No cinematic grade, no film grain, no vignette, no slow motion.

[3] ASSET ROLES
The start image controls the woman's identity, her cream knit sweater and dark jeans, the aisle, the shelving and the lighting. @Image 1 controls ONLY the look of the product pallet the pan lands on: a tall stack of DARK-GREEN cartons with a red banner and a white projector illustration, with red poinsettia and garland on top. Do not copy camera angle or lighting from @Image 1. @Video 1 controls ONLY the camera path and the rhythm of the performance: walk, stop, hand to mouth, point, whip pan right, settle on the product stack. Do not copy the woman, her clothes, the trolley colour, the store or the boxes from @Video 1. @Video 1 is silent - there is no audio, no music and no soundtrack in it to copy.

[4] CHARACTERS
THE WOMAN - long light-brown hair, cream oatmeal knit sweater, dark jeans, seen from behind and slightly to her left. COUNT LOCK: exactly one person on screen for all 4 seconds. No other shoppers, no staff, no children.

[5] LOCATION - every one of these exists in the start image and must survive to the last frame before the pan: a wide polished pale-floor supermarket aisle; decorated Christmas trees with red and gold ornaments standing on top of the left-hand shelves; red baubles hanging from the ceiling; red-accented shelving on the right. THE TROLLEY - the dark grey shopping trolley she is pushing.

[6] FIRST FRAME - exactly the start image: THE WOMAN from behind and slightly left, both hands on THE TROLLEY handle, mid-aisle, walking away from camera.

[7] TIMELINE
0.0-1.0s - camera handheld, follows THE WOMAN from behind at walking pace; THE WOMAN pushes THE TROLLEY forward two steps.
1.0-2.0s - THE WOMAN releases the handle and takes one step forward ahead of THE TROLLEY. THE TROLLEY keeps rolling forward on its own down the aisle, unpushed. Her right hand flies up and covers her mouth; her head turns to her right; her shoulders lift. Camera holds.
2.0-3.0s - THE WOMAN drops the hand from her mouth and throws her right arm straight out, index finger pointing forward and to the right, off the right edge of frame. THE WOMAN speaks. Camera holds.
3.0-4.0s - as her arm reaches full extension the camera WHIP PANS hard to the right with heavy horizontal motion blur; THE WOMAN leaves frame to the left; the pan decelerates and settles on the tall pallet of DARK-GREEN product cartons from @Image 1 standing in the aisle with red poinsettia and garland on top. Tiny push-in and hold.

[8] DIALOGUE
English dialogue. THE WOMAN: "There is no way!" Spoken 2.1-2.9s. Delivery: loud, delighted, genuinely stunned, American accent. This spoken line is the ONLY voice in the clip. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

[9] CAMERA AND OPTICS - single continuous handheld take, vertical 9:16, normal wide-angle phone lens, chest height, about two metres behind THE WOMAN, her body in the centre-left third. One camera movement only: the whip pan right at 3.0s. Do not cut. Do not zoom. Do not orbit. No fisheye, no barrel distortion, no warped shelving or curved floor lines.

[10] LIGHTING - flat overhead retail lighting with warm pools under the decorations, clean white balance, no colour cast change across the clip.

[11] PHYSICS - THE TROLLEY rolls straight and slows gradually under its own momentum after she lets go; it never turns, never tips, never leaves the floor, never stops dead. Her sweater and hair move naturally with her turn.

[12] AUDIO - DRY DOCUMENTARY AUDIO ONLY. The track contains exactly three things and nothing else: low supermarket room ambience, the rattle of trolley wheels on the hard floor, and her single spoken line. Total silence apart from those. NO MUSIC, NO SONG, NO SCORE, NO SOUNDTRACK, NO INSTRUMENTS.

[13] POSITIVE LOCKS - exactly one person. THE TROLLEY continues forward alone after 1.0s. The aisle, the decorated trees on the shelf tops and the hanging red baubles are present in every frame before the pan. The pan lands on cartons that are DARK GREEN with a red banner.
BANNED: any music, any song, any score, any soundtrack, any instrument, any singing; a second shopper, the trolley stopping dead or vanishing, THE WOMAN turning to face the camera, any cut, blue or white or brown or kraft boxes, a shelf of unrelated products, subtitles, on-screen text, slow motion, any blur outside the pan.

image.label: Image prompt — Frame 1, the family walk
image.text:
Copy the attached reference photo EXACTLY: same camera position, same camera height, same lens, same distance, same vertical 9:16 framing, same wide bright big-box store walkway receding into depth behind them, same glossy pale polished floor, same three people walking TOWARD the camera at full length with their feet visible, same arrangement - one adult on the left, one adult on the right, a small young child in the middle between them - same relaxed walking stride. Change only three things.

FIRST - THE PEOPLE. A completely different family. The man is now about 36, dark hair, short beard, in a charcoal half-zip knit sweater, dark jeans and white sneakers, walking on the LEFT. The woman is now about 34, light brown hair worn down, in a cream ribbed knit jumper under an open camel wool coat, dark jeans and tan ankle boots, walking on the RIGHT. Natural everyday faces, no makeup look, warm easy smiles. BOTH ADULTS ARE LOOKING AROUND THE STORE, NOT AT THE CAMERA AND NOT AT THE CHILD: the man's head is turned to his left, looking off at the dressed display tables and the decorated trees on that side, and the woman's head is turned to her right, looking off at the trees and the gift boxes on her side, both with relaxed easy smiles as they browse. Neither of them looks down at the child and neither face is turned toward the lens - no eye contact with the camera from either adult, and neither of them is looking at the boy. Between them a small toddler boy of about three, the same young age and the same small height as the child in the reference photo - a little one who only comes up to the adults' hips, with soft round toddler cheeks and short fine light brown hair - in a red and cream knitted Christmas jumper, dark jeans and tiny white trainers, walking forward on his own with BOTH of his own small hands held together low in front of his chest, one hand just above the other, his elbows in at his sides, the same hold as the child in the reference photo. Held in both of those little hands at once is the SAME DRINK AS THE CHILD IN THE REFERENCE PHOTO: a tall clear plastic takeaway cold-cup full of bright green iced matcha. The drink is a vivid opaque grass-green matcha latte filling the cup to the top with a slightly frothy green surface, the cup is smooth clear plastic, no lid and no straw, roughly as tall as the child's two hands stacked together. BOTH of his small hands are wrapped right around the cup, one hand just above the other, fingers curled around the sides, thumbs up, elbows tucked in at his sides, the cup held upright and low against his tummy and tucked in close to his body - the exact same cup, the exact same green drink and the exact same two-handed hold as the child in the reference photo - and he is looking down at it. Both of his hands are on that cup and neither of them is holding an adult. He is NOT holding a pen, NOT holding a stick, NOT holding a toy, NOT holding a candle - it is a green matcha drink in a clear cup. THE TWO ADULTS HOLD EACH OTHER'S HAND: the man's right hand and the woman's left hand are clasped together above and slightly behind the child's head, their joined hands clearly visible, and their outer hands hang relaxed at their sides. Same poses, same stride, same positions, same scale as the reference.

SECOND - THE STORE. A different Christmas store: a warm homeware department rather than the reference's store - a wide central walkway, waist-high display tables on both sides dressed with red and gold gift boxes and stacked cushions, tall shelving only along the LEFT side behind them - the RIGHT side of the frame has NO shelving of any kind: no shelf units, no racks, no gondola shelving, no stacked shelf bays, nothing shelf-like anywhere on the right, just decorated Christmas trees, a low display table and open store space on that side, three decorated Christmas trees set back along each side with warm white fairy lights and red and gold baubles, thick pine garland along the display edges, a bright clean white ceiling with recessed downlights.

THIRD - THE FRAMING, and this is the important one. The whole family sits LOWER in the frame than in the reference. The top QUARTER of the picture is clean calm background only - plain bright ceiling and the soft upper wall of the store - with nothing hanging into it: no baubles, no signage, no garland, no banners, no lettering, no heads. Both adults' heads begin only BELOW that clean top quarter. Keep all three of them full length with their feet and the floor still visible at the bottom edge. Do not shrink the people to achieve this and do not crop their feet - lower the camera slightly and leave the clean band above them.

Everything else in the frame stays identical to the reference. Shot on an iPhone 16 Pro. HYPERREALISTIC - an ordinary real photograph of real people, indistinguishable from a candid family snapshot taken in a real shop: real skin with visible pores and fine texture, real stray hairs, real fabric weave and pilling in the knitwear, real creases in the denim, real scuffs on the trainers, natural skin tones with no smoothing and no retouching, believable imperfect faces. Extremely high quality, tack-sharp focus edge to edge, crisp fine detail in the knitwear and the faces, perfect natural realistic store lighting with soft realistic shadows under the feet, perfectly exposed, zero motion blur, nothing blurry or soft. NOT illustration, NOT 3D render, NOT CGI, NOT AI-looking, no plastic skin, no waxy faces, no airbrushed glow, no painterly or stylised look. Normal wide-angle lens, straight vertical lines, no fisheye distortion.

No text, no captions, no watermarks, no logos, no lettering anywhere in the image.

clip.label: Clip prompt — the one in the cut
clip.text:
AUDIO RULE - HIGHEST PRIORITY, READ THIS FIRST: this clip has NO MUSIC OF ANY KIND. No background song, no soundtrack, no score, no melody, no instruments, no singing, no humming, no jingle, no Christmas song, no festive music bed, no ambient musical pad, no strings, no piano, no bells used as music. The audio track contains ONLY real natural sound recorded in that shop, plus the one line of toddler speech written in the AUDIO block. @Video 1 has no audio track at all - import no sound whatsoever from it. If any music appears anywhere in the 5 seconds the clip is wrong.

ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE - SECOND MOST IMPORTANT: this is a single unbroken 5-second phone take. There is no cut, no edit, no transition, no jump, no fade and no change of shot at any point. The child's body keeps moving through every beat boundary - she is already beginning to turn away while the parents are still reacting, and she is already walking while she finishes turning. No beat ever starts from a standstill.

TASK: image-to-video. The start image is frame 0.0s. Hold its shop, its floor, its decorated trees and display tables, its shelving, its people, their clothes and its lighting exactly.

[1] SUMMARY
A toddler walking through a bright Christmas homeware shop between her parents lets go of her iced matcha; it hits the floor and bursts, the parents stop and stare down at her in shock, and she turns and walks away up the aisle to a pyramid of green Christmas-projector cartons and throws both arms up at it. 5 seconds, one continuous handheld phone take, vertical.

[2] GLOBAL STYLE
Crisp real iPhone footage, handheld, real-time speed, bright even shop lighting. Sharp and in focus from the first frame to the last, at least as sharp as the start image. No blur, no haze, no soft focus, no cinematic grade, no grain, no slow motion, no speed ramp.

[3] ASSET ROLES
The start image is frame 0.0s and controls the shop, the polished pale floor, the decorated trees and dressed display tables on both sides, the shelving on the left, the three people, their faces, their clothes and the light.
@Image 1 controls ONLY what the end of the clip arrives at: the pyramid stack of our green cartons on its red platform, the decorated tree beside it, and the child seen from behind with both arms raised in front of it.
@Video 1 controls ONLY movement and camera: the way the cup is released and falls, the way the drink bursts on the floor, the way the child turns her back and walks away up the aisle, and the way the camera follows her from behind and drifts right onto the display. Take nothing else from @Video 1 - not its shop, not its shelves, not its people, not their clothes, not its colours, not its lighting.
IMPORTANT DIVERGENCE FROM @Video 1: in @Video 1 the two adults walk on past the camera and never react. In THIS clip they DO react - they stop dead and stare down at the child in shock. Do not copy their non-reaction from @Video 1.

[4] CHARACTERS
THE CHILD - one small girl about 3, red-and-cream knitted Christmas jumper, dark jeans, tiny white trainers, centre of frame between the two adults. At 0.0s both of her hands are cupped low against her tummy around a tall clear plastic cold-cup of bright green iced matcha with a domed lid.
THE FATHER - a man about 36 on the LEFT, charcoal half-zip, dark jeans, white sneakers.
THE MOTHER - a woman about 34 on the RIGHT, cream ribbed jumper under an open camel coat, dark jeans, tan ankle boots.
Their inner hands are clasped together above and behind the child. COUNT LOCK: exactly three people in the foreground. No fourth family member, no staff member walking into shot.

[5] OBJECTS
THE CUP - a tall clear plastic cold-cup of bright green iced matcha with a domed lid. It is a DRINK. It is not a match, not a matchstick, not a candle, not a stick of any kind.
THE DISPLAY - a pyramid stack of our tall forest-green tuck-top cartons on a low red platform, four tiers high, each carton printed with a dark red band, a gold BRANDA wordmark and a cream serif CHRISTMAS LIGHT PROJECTOR headline. It stands on the RIGHT side of the aisle ahead, with a decorated Christmas tree beside it, exactly as in @Image 1.

[6] LOCATION - a bright Christmas homeware shop: a glossy pale floor, decorated Christmas trees and dressed display tables down both sides, tall shelving on the LEFT only, warm shop lighting. All of it survives to the last frame. The top quarter of the frame stays clean and uncluttered.

[7] FIRST FRAME - exactly the start image: the three of them mid-stride walking toward camera, the child between them holding THE CUP low in both hands, her head tipped up.

[8] TIMELINE
0.0-0.5s - the camera is near-static at child height. All three keep walking toward camera in stride. THE CHILD is already looking up and forward.
0.5-0.9s - THE CHILD's fingers open and she lets go. THE CUP drops straight down between her feet, lid first, turning once as it falls.
0.9-1.5s - THE CUP hits the polished floor and bursts: a wide bright green splat spreads out across the pale floor, ice cubes skid away, the domed lid pops off and spins flat. THE CHILD's arms drop open at her sides and she looks down at it, mouth open.
1.2-2.0s - both adults stop dead mid-stride, their clasped hands pulling apart, and snap their heads DOWN to look at the child and the green splat. Their faces are SHOCKED - eyes wide, eyebrows up, mouths open; THE MOTHER's free hand comes up to her mouth, THE FATHER's shoulders drop. They stay where they are and keep staring down.
2.0-2.5s - while they are still staring, THE CHILD turns her back to the camera in one continuous movement, already lifting her leading foot into the first step.
2.5-4.0s - THE CHILD walks away from camera up the aisle into depth, arms swinging, unbothered. The camera follows her from behind at her height with a natural handheld bounce, and drifts slightly RIGHT so THE DISPLAY comes into frame on the right. The parents fall away behind, still stopped.
4.0-5.0s - THE CHILD reaches THE DISPLAY, stops in front of it and throws BOTH arms straight up toward the third and fourth tiers of cartons, hands open, tipping her head back. She says her line here. The camera settles on her from behind with THE DISPLAY filling the right of frame, exactly the composition of @Image 1. The last frame holds on that.

[9] CAMERA AND OPTICS - vertical 9:16, normal wide-angle phone lens at roughly child height. One continuous handheld take with a natural walking bounce: near-static for the first two seconds, then a follow from behind with a slight rightward drift onto THE DISPLAY. Normal wide-angle only - no fisheye, no barrel distortion, no curved shelving lines. No cut, no zoom, no orbit.

[10] LIGHTING - bright even warm shop lighting, unchanged for the whole clip.

[11] PHYSICS - THE CUP is a light plastic cup of cold liquid: it falls fast under real gravity, lands with a slap, and the drink bursts outward low and wide across the hard floor. The green splat is a shallow spill that stays on the floor; it does not fountain upward, does not splash onto the child or the adults, and does not reach their knees. The ice skids, it does not bounce high. Nothing flies up out of frame.

[12] AUDIO - natural sound only: the flat hard slap of a plastic cup hitting a polished floor, the wet spread of liquid, ice skittering, quiet shop ambience and distant footsteps. At 4.2s THE CHILD says clearly in a small toddler voice: "Mama, I want it!" Nothing else is spoken. (no BGM). No subtitles.

[13] POSITIVE LOCKS - real-time motion at normal speed throughout. Exactly three people. One continuous take with no cut. THE CUP is a green iced drink. The adults stop and stare down in shock. THE CHILD ends in front of the pyramid of green cartons with both arms raised, seen from behind. The picture stays sharp to the last frame.
DO NOT INCLUDE: any music, any song, any score, any soundtrack; a cut, an edit, a transition, a fade or a second shot; slow motion; the adults walking on past without reacting; the adults kneeling down, picking the cup up, cleaning the floor or scolding her; the liquid splashing high, hitting the people, or reaching above knee height; the child crying; the child holding a match, a matchstick, a candle or a stick; a fourth person; the camera overtaking or getting in front of the child; on-screen text; subtitles.

Every word rigid, sharp, correctly spelled, never warped.

clip.text:
Animate the reference image exactly as it is. Warehouse-club aisle, pallet stack of black LED CURTAIN LIGHTS boxes, woman in the red parka standing in the middle of the aisle.

CAMERA - HELD IPHONE, LOCKED FRAMING: a handheld iPhone shot filmed by a shopper standing in the aisle. NO zoom in, NO zoom out, NO push-in, NO pull-back, NO pan, NO tilt, NO dolly, NO crop. The framing does not change for the entire 5 seconds - only the tiny natural micro-drift and micro-shake of a real human hand holding a phone. One single continuous unbroken take, no cut, no jump, no reset.

WHAT MOVES - EVERY SINGLE PERSON RUSHES TOWARD THE PALLET OF BOXES: this is a stampede onto the product. Shoppers pour in from the left edge, the right edge and the far end of the aisle and converge on the pallet stack in the middle of frame. Every person in the shot is moving TOWARD the pallet. Arms shoot out over each other's shoulders, hands snatch black boxes off the stack, two people grab the same box and pull, a man hugs three boxes to his chest and turns straight back to the stack for a fourth, a woman reaches over the top of the pile on tiptoe, someone pushes in from behind and the crowd compresses tighter around the pallet. The woman in the red parka lunges forward onto the pallet with both arms, seizes a black box off the top of the stack, clamps it against her chest and screams with a wild delighted open-mouthed grin, then immediately reaches back in for another one. Everybody is shouting and screaming at once, faces frantic and excited. The pallet loses boxes fast but never empties completely.

There is no chase, nobody is running from anybody, nobody looks frightened. Every body in frame is pushing INWARD toward the boxes. Nobody loads a box into a shopping cart or trolley, nobody wheels a cart away - the boxes are grabbed and held in people's arms only.

DO NOT CHANGE: the aisle, the steel shelving, the concrete floor, the overhead warehouse lighting, the signage, the red cart handle in the bottom-right corner of frame.

clip.label: Clip prompt — the one in the cut
clip.text:
Real home video, shot on a hand-held iPhone by a person standing in the room a few steps behind her, phone held upright at chest height. One continuous shot. The camera stays in exactly the same spot for the whole clip with only tiny natural hand sway and micro-jitter - the small live breathing wobble of real hand-held phone footage, never a steady locked-off tripod look. It does not reframe, does not follow her, does not tilt, pan, zoom or push in. No phone, hand, fingers, thumb or arm ever appears in the foreground.

HARD RULE, THIS ONE FIRST: the whole clip is ONE single unbroken shot from the first frame to the last. No cut, no jump cut, no second angle, no scene change, no transition, no dissolve at any point. The motion runs continuously - every moment grows out of the moment before it, and her body never resets, jumps position or teleports between one part and the next.

For the first second she is just taping the inflatable Santa to the ceiling - both hands up, pressing and smoothing, nothing dramatic.

Then, without any pause or break in the movement, she loses her footing and falls off the ladder to the floor. Her arms are still up and still coming down out of the taping motion as her balance goes - the taping and the fall are one unbroken piece of movement, not two separate actions.

The fall has real weight. An ordinary woman's balance goes, gravity takes her, and she is on the floor in well under a second - fast, heavy, a bit ugly, exactly like real footage of someone coming off a ladder. Her limbs are heavy and human, not floaty or rubbery, and she never hangs in the air. The ladder goes over with her and clatters onto the rug.

She lands hard and the movement carries straight on into stillness without a break - she settles, rocks slightly as her weight comes to rest, and stays down on the floor for the rest of the clip, not moving much, just stunned and breathing. Her chest is still moving and she is still there when the clip ends.

The inflatable Santa stays taped to the ceiling the whole time.

No slow motion. No speed ramp, no speed change of any kind - the clip plays at one constant real-time speed from start to finish. No zoom, no push-in, no pan, no tilt. No captions or text.

Audio: room tone only, no music - the tape, a short gasp, the ladder hitting the floor, then her breathing.

image.label: Image prompt — the starting frame, take 5
image.text:
Extremely high quality candid vertical iPhone photo taken from the floor of a double-height Christmas living room, looking up and across at a woman standing on the mezzanine landing, evening. We see her from below and slightly to the side, her raised arms and the high ceiling in front of her.

FRAMING AND ANGLE: the camera stands on the living-room floor MUCH closer in to the stairs than a wide establishing shot, tilted up, so the woman and the inflatable she is taping fill most of the picture and the room reads as context around them rather than as the subject. The mezzanine landing crosses the frame with its black metal railing along it, and the woman stands on that landing behind the railing DEAD CENTRE on the vertical axis of the frame, framed from roughly the waist up and very large in the picture - she is the biggest thing in the photograph and the taped inflatable is directly above and ahead of her, also near the centre, so her reaching arm and the inflatable together sit in the middle of the frame. A short stretch of the open white staircase still enters the lower right corner, and the living-room floor is still clearly visible below her in the lower part of the picture, so the drop from the landing to the floor reads plainly. She is NOT on a ladder - there is no ladder anywhere in the picture.

THE KEY ELEMENT: a large inflatable Santa Claus decoration is TAPED FLAT TO THE HIGH WHITE CEILING above the double-height space, lying on its back against the plaster and facing down into the room, held by a mess of criss-crossed silver duct tape strips over its legs, arms and hat. It is clearly fixed to the ceiling. It hangs out over the open double-height void rather than over the landing. One corner has started to peel, with a long strip of tape hanging down.

HER POSE - THIS IS THE POINT OF THE PICTURE: she is leaning far out over the landing railing to reach it. Her hips are pressed against the top rail, her weight is tipped forward past it and out over the open void, her feet still on the landing behind her with her heels lifting, one hand gripping the rail and the other stretched up and out pressing a fresh strip of silver duct tape onto Santa's shoulder, a roll of duct tape in her gripping hand. She is visibly overreaching and off balance, the rail the only thing holding her, empty air and the floor below her.

THE ROOM - COPY IT FROM THE FIRST ATTACHED PHOTOGRAPH: the room in this picture is the EXACT SAME ROOM as the first attached photograph, same house, same light, same furniture in the same places - a double-height white modern American farmhouse living room - white painted walls, a wall of tall black-framed windows at the right with a dark winter garden behind them, a white open-tread staircase with slim black metal spindles, a mezzanine landing with a matching black rail and a green garland with red bows wound along it, a white plaster fireplace on the ground floor, a tall green Christmas tree with warm white lights and red and gold baubles standing in the double-height space, pale wide-plank oak floor, a light linen sofa and a cream rug.

A UNITED STATES FLAG: a real fabric United States flag hangs flat against the white wall in the background under the landing, clearly readable stars and stripes, hanging straight and still, about the size of a large poster. It does not cover the Christmas tree or the fireplace and it does not reach up into the empty band of ceiling at the top of the frame.

HER CLOTHES: matching American-flag Christmas pyjamas - a pyjama top with bold red and white horizontal stripes and a navy blue yoke across the shoulders covered in small white stars, and matching red and white striped pyjama bottoms, soft brushed cotton, slightly loose the way real pyjamas fit - with thick grey wool socks. She is mid 30s with dark brown hair in a loose low bun.

There is no projected light anywhere - the ceiling, the walls and the staircase are plain painted plaster and plain timber, completely clean, no projected patterns, no snowflakes, no stars, no coloured light spilling on any surface. The room is lit only by the Christmas tree, the fireplace and ordinary warm lamps.

COLOUR - READ THIS CAREFULLY: neutral white balance, the way an iPhone auto-corrects a warm room. The picture is NOT orange, NOT amber, NOT sepia, NOT golden-hour, and there is no warm colour cast laid over the whole frame. The ceiling and the walls read as clean white paint, the window frames and the rail read as true black, the oak floor reads as natural wood, the flag keeps true red, white and navy. The Christmas tree lights, the fireplace and the lamps are warm points of light sitting inside a neutrally balanced room - they do not tint the rest of the picture.

LIGHTING AND QUALITY: bright, clean and evenly lit - plenty of light on the high ceiling, on the landing and on her, no dark corners, no heavy shadows. Shot on an iPhone and straight out of the camera roll: an ordinary everyday snapshot, not a magazine photo and not a rendered image. Modern phone-camera look - wide dynamic range, lifted shadows, clean highlights, accurate colour. Extremely high quality, tack sharp and in focus everywhere, crisp detail in the duct tape, the inflatable vinyl sheen and the weave of her pyjamas, realistic skin and fabric texture. Absolutely nothing blurry: no motion blur, no soft focus, no background blur, no grain, no film look, no cinematic grade, no vignette, no bloom. Normal wide-angle lens, vertical lines vertical and parallel, no fisheye distortion.

FRAMING: leave a generous clean band of plain empty ceiling across the very top of the image - roughly the top fifth of the frame - completely empty and free of Santa, of tape, of beams, of garland and of any other object, so a caption can sit there. Make that room by tilting the camera up slightly, NOT by pulling the camera back and NOT by shrinking the woman - she stays close and large and centred exactly as described above.

No captions, no watermarks, no lettering anywhere in the image.

clip.label: Clip prompt — the one in the cut
clip.text:
Single continuous handheld iPhone shot, 5 seconds, vertical 9:16, filmed by someone standing on the living room floor below and holding the phone up — real held-phone look with natural handheld sway, no cuts, no zoom, no lens push-in, framing locked exactly as in the start frame for the whole clip.

Start frame: a woman in American-flag pajamas stands on the upstairs balcony, leaning her hips against the dark wooden top rail, both arms stretched up over her head, pressing strips of silver duct tape onto the white ceiling to hold up a big inflatable Santa. Below her: the two-storey living room with the lit fireplace, the American flag on the wall, the decorated Christmas tree and the white sofa.

ACTION TIMELINE:
0.0–1.0s — Up on her toes, she smooths one more strip of silver tape onto the ceiling with her palm, then gives the inflatable Santa a quick test tug to check it is holding, leaning her whole weight forward into the wooden top rail.
1.0–1.5s — The section of the dark wooden top rail she is leaning on splits with a loud crack and swings away from her, and she pitches forward over the balcony edge, eyes wide, both hands clamping onto the inflatable Santa.
1.5–2.5s — She drops down into the living room, the inflatable Santa peeling straight off the ceiling and coming with her — the silver tape strips tearing free and trailing, the green garland and a red bow sliding off the broken rail behind her.
2.5–3.4s — She misses the sofa completely and lands flat on her back on the wooden living room floor in front of it, hitting the floor and settling straight down with no bounce, and the big inflatable Santa flops down on top of her, covering her from the waist up.
3.4–5.0s — She shoves the inflatable Santa's head sideways off her face, hair everywhere, looks straight up at the camera and bursts out laughing, still flat on her back on the floor with the Santa across her lap. End frame: her laughing on the floor under the inflatable, the empty broken balcony rail above her.

AUDIO: her real voice, lip-synced, matching her appearance — a short surprised yelp as the rail gives way, then breathless laughing at the end; the sharp crack of splitting wood; duct tape ripping off the ceiling; the squeaky rubbery scuff of the big inflatable; the heavy flat thud of her body landing on the wooden floor; the fireplace crackling quietly under everything. (no BGM). No subtitles.

REALISM — HARD RULES: she keeps exactly the same face, hair and American-flag pajamas as the start frame the whole clip. The living room stays pixel-faithful to the start frame — same fireplace, same flag, same Christmas tree, same sofa, same windows, same warm lamp light. The inflatable Santa stays the same size, colours and printed face the whole clip and never deforms into a different character. Real weight and gravity on the fall — she drops straight down, she is never thrown or launched sideways. She lands on the wooden floor, NOT on the sofa - she never touches the sofa at any point in the clip. Real phone-camera look, slight sensor noise, mild motion blur on the fall, no cinematic bokeh, no slow motion, no text overlays, no watermark.

POSITIVE LOCKS: everything plays at real-time speed. One continuous take from 0.0s to 5.0s. The camera never moves from where it is in the start frame.

clip.label: Clip prompt — the one in the cut
clip.text:
Single continuous handheld iPhone shot, 5 seconds, vertical 9:16, filmed by someone standing on the hallway floor holding the phone up — real held-phone look with natural handheld sway, no cuts, no zoom, no lens push-in, framing locked exactly as in the start frame for the whole clip.

Start frame: a woman in American-flag pajamas stands on the staircase behind the dark wooden railing, leaning out over it with one arm stretched up to the gold star on top of the tall decorated Christmas tree beside the stairs. Two small children in matching American-flag pajamas stand on the floor at the lower left of the frame with their backs to the camera, watching her. Wrapped presents at the foot of the tree.

ACTION TIMELINE:
0.0–1.0s — Both hands now on the gold star, she works it down onto the top of the tree, stretching further and further out over the railing, more and more of her weight going onto the tree itself.
1.0–1.6s — The tree tips. It leans away from the stairs toward the open floor and keeps going, and she loses her balance and comes over the railing with it, still holding on. At the same instant the two children take three quick steps further to the left, well out of the way, and stop there — the tree never comes near them.
1.6–2.4s — The whole tree swings down diagonally across the frame and crashes flat onto the wooden floor, branches flattening, the gold star snapping off the top and skittering away on its own.
2.4–3.2s — She lands on the floor face-down across the fallen tree, and the impact bursts a wave of ornaments off the branches — dozens of red, gold, pink and white baubles bouncing out low across the wooden floor and rolling toward the camera, spreading right across the bottom of the frame.
3.2–5.0s — The last ornaments wobble to a stop on the floor. She lies still across the fallen tree for a beat, then lifts her head, blows the hair out of her face and starts laughing. The two children stay where they moved to on the left, staring at the mess. End frame: the tree flat on the floor, ornaments scattered everywhere, her looking up laughing.

AUDIO: her real voice, lip-synced, matching her appearance — a short yelp as she goes over, then breathless laughing at the end; the dry rush of the tree branches going over; the heavy thud of the tree hitting the wooden floor; dozens of glass and plastic ornaments clattering, bouncing and rolling on hard wood; one small surprised squeal from a child. (no BGM). No subtitles.

REALISM — HARD RULES: she keeps exactly the same face, hair and American-flag pajamas as the start frame the whole clip, and the two children keep exactly the same clothes and size. The hallway stays pixel-faithful to the start frame — same staircase, same dark wooden railing and newel post, same American flag on the wall, same wooden floor, same daylight. The children are never touched by the tree and are never underneath it. Real weight and gravity — the tree topples on its own mass and stops on the floor, she drops straight down, nobody is thrown or launched. Real phone-camera look, slight sensor noise, mild motion blur on the fall, no cinematic bokeh, no slow motion, no text overlays, no watermark. No subtitles, no captions and no on-screen words of any kind anywhere in the picture.

POSITIVE LOCKS: everything plays at real-time speed. One continuous take from 0.0s to 5.0s. The camera never moves from where it is in the start frame.

notes.text: The owner on take 1: “Came out very bad, the ai kinda combined these 2 clips. This time don't add any reference video.” Take 2 removed the reference and passed. clip.label: Clip prompt — COPY THIS ONE · v22_c01_g1.mp4
clip.text:
Single continuous handheld iPhone shot, 5 seconds, vertical 9:16, hyperrealistic. No cuts, no zoom, no slow motion, no speed ramp. The camera itself IS the phone being held by a man standing in the hallway doorway, so we see ONLY what he sees. No phone, no screen, no hand, no fingers, no thumb, no arm, no sleeve, no device and no object ever appears in the foreground or along any edge of the frame.

Start frame: a red-haired mother in a navy-blue cable-knit sweater kneels on dark wooden floorboards in the lower left, her right arm stretched out to a white wall socket on the white corner at the right of the frame, holding the plug of a big tangled knot of unlit multicoloured Christmas string lights that lies on the floor beside her. One continuous run of that same string leads away across the floor and up into the decorated but unlit Christmas tree standing on the right. A boy in green-and-white striped pyjamas and a small girl in a pale pink nightgown stand behind her near the cream linen sofa.

ACTION TIMELINE:
0.0-0.8s - The mother pushes the plug the last few centimetres into the socket. Her hand moves slowly and steadily, her head still turned in profile watching it. Everything else in the room is calm and still. The tree is dark. The camera is locked where it stands in the start frame, only natural handheld sway.

AT 0.8s - ONE SINGLE INSTANT, AND EVERYTHING IN IT HAPPENS ON THE SAME FRAME. The two pins seat in the socket; every bulb on the knot and on the tree flashes on for a split second; and in that same instant a burst of orange flame erupts low in the Christmas tree where the string meets the branches and the tree catches fire. On that exact same frame the man holding the camera shouts "Oh, shoot" and the whole frame jolts as he flinches backwards. The fire is not delayed, it does not build up, it does not start small and grow for a second first - the tree is already burning on the same frame the plug goes in.

0.8-2.0s - The flames climb the tree fast and realistically, running up through the dry branches, orange and yellow, throwing real flickering firelight across the warm white lime-plaster walls, the floorboards, the sofa and the three faces, with dark smoke rolling up off the top of the tree toward the ceiling. Ornaments glow and the branches blacken. The mother recoils hard away from the socket, twists round onto her hands and pushes herself up off the floor. The boy and the girl scream and turn toward the camera. The man with the camera takes ONLY TWO OR THREE SHORT STEPS BACKWARDS and then stops and stands his ground. That small retreat is finished by about 1.6s. He does not walk backwards down the hallway, he does not run, he does not retreat any further at any later point in the clip.

2.0-5.0s - The camera is now STANDING STILL in the hallway just behind the doorway, holding its position with only natural handheld sway, not moving backwards at all. The mother is on her feet and runs straight toward the camera with her arms out, scooping the two children ahead of her, all three sprinting toward the lens and growing rapidly larger in the frame, faces wide with panic, the boy's arms pumping, the little girl half carried. Because the camera is no longer backing away, they close the distance fast and come right up to the lens. End frame: the three of them very close and very large in the frame mid-run, almost filling it, the burning tree bright behind them through the doorway.

AUDIO: natural room sound only. One male voice, off camera behind the lens, shouting "Oh, shoot" exactly on the frame the tree catches fire - nothing else from him before it, nothing else after it. Then the crackle and roar of the fire, the mother shouting wordlessly, the two children screaming, bare feet running on wood. NO music, no score, no background song, no narration, no added sound effects beyond these.

REALISM - HARD RULES: the mother, the boy and the girl keep exactly the same faces, hair, clothes and body shapes as the start frame throughout. The room stays the same room - same warm white lime-plaster walls and tiled skirting band, same cream linen sofa with the rust-and-ivory blanket, same dark oak floorboards, same rug, same lamp, same window. clip.text:
Single continuous handheld iPhone shot, 5 seconds, vertical 9:16, hyperrealistic. No cuts, no zoom, no slow motion, no speed ramp. The camera itself IS the phone being held by a man standing in the hallway doorway, so we see ONLY what he sees. No phone, no screen, no hand, no fingers, no thumb, no arm, no sleeve, no device and no object ever appears in the foreground or along any edge of the frame.

Start frame: a blonde mother in a forest-green cable-knit sweater kneels on pale wooden floorboards in the lower left, her right arm stretched out to a white wall socket on the white corner at the right of the frame, holding the plug of a big tangled knot of unlit multicoloured Christmas string lights that lies on the floor beside her. One continuous run of that same string leads away across the floor and up into the decorated but unlit Christmas tree standing on the right. A boy in red-and-white striped pyjamas and a small girl in a cream nightgown stand behind her near the navy sofa.

ACTION TIMELINE:
0.0-0.8s - The mother pushes the plug the last few centimetres into the socket. Her hand moves slowly and steadily, her head still turned in profile watching it. Everything else in the room is calm and still. The tree is dark. The camera is locked where it stands in the start frame, only natural handheld sway.

AT 0.8s - ONE SINGLE INSTANT, AND EVERYTHING IN IT HAPPENS ON THE SAME FRAME. The two pins seat in the socket; every bulb on the knot and on the tree flashes on for a split second; and in that same instant a burst of orange flame erupts low in the Christmas tree where the string meets the branches and the tree catches fire. On that exact same frame the man holding the camera shouts "Oh, shoot" and the whole frame jolts as he flinches backwards. The fire is not delayed, it does not build up, it does not start small and grow for a second first - the tree is already burning on the same frame the plug goes in.

0.8-2.0s - The flames climb the tree fast and realistically, running up through the dry branches, orange and yellow, throwing real flickering firelight across the shiplap walls, the floorboards, the sofa and the three faces, with dark smoke rolling up off the top of the tree toward the ceiling. Ornaments glow and the branches blacken. The mother recoils hard away from the socket, twists round onto her hands and pushes herself up off the floor. The boy and the girl scream and turn toward the camera. The man with the camera takes ONLY TWO OR THREE SHORT STEPS BACKWARDS and then stops and stands his ground. That small retreat is finished by about 1.6s. He does not walk backwards down the hallway, he does not run, he does not retreat any further at any later point in the clip.

2.0-5.0s - The camera is now STANDING STILL in the hallway just behind the doorway, holding its position with only natural handheld sway, not moving backwards at all. The mother is on her feet and runs straight toward the camera with her arms out, scooping the two children ahead of her, all three sprinting toward the lens and growing rapidly larger in the frame, faces wide with panic, the boy's arms pumping, the little girl half carried. Because the camera is no longer backing away, they close the distance fast and come right up to the lens. End frame: the three of them very close and very large in the frame mid-run, almost filling it, the burning tree bright behind them through the doorway.

AUDIO: natural room sound only. One male voice, off camera behind the lens, shouting "Oh, shoot" exactly on the frame the tree catches fire - nothing else from him before it, nothing else after it. Then the crackle and roar of the fire, the mother shouting wordlessly, the two children screaming, bare feet running on wood. NO music, no score, no background song, no narration, no added sound effects beyond these.

REALISM - HARD RULES: the mother, the boy and the girl keep exactly the same faces, hair, clothes and body shapes as the start frame throughout. The room stays the same room - same cream shiplap walls, same navy sofa with the mustard blanket, same pale floorboards, same rug, same lamp, same window. The fire behaves like real fire on a real dry conifer: it spreads along branches, it does not float, it does not appear as a glowing overlay, it casts real moving light and real shadows on every surface, and it produces real dark smoke. Real phone-camera look with slight sensor noise and natural motion blur only from the handheld movement. No text overlays, no captions, no watermark, no on-screen graphics.

POSITIVE LOCKS: one continuous take from 0.0s to 5.0s with no cut anywhere. Everything plays at real-time speed. The camera never zooms. The ONLY camera movement in the entire clip is a short backwards flinch of two or three steps between 0.8s and 1.6s; before 0.8s the camera holds its start-frame position and after 1.6s the camera holds its new position and stays there until the end. BANNED: the camera walking or running backwards down the hallway, the camera retreating for more than three steps, the camera moving away from the family during their run, the family staying the same size in the frame as they run. Nobody stops moving once the fire starts.

notes.title: Worked — variation lives only in the cast and the set
notes.text: Across all four videos FRAMING AND ANGLE, THE KNOT AND THE PLUG, THE CONNECTION, THE TREE IS NOT SWITCHED ON, LIGHTING AND QUALITY and the caption band are the same bytes ; only THE ROOM, THE TREE, THE MOTHER, THE CHILDREN and one COLOUR clause ever changed. notes.text: v12, v17 and v22 all attached v9_c01_g8.png as @Image 1, and all three frames and all three clips passed first take. Chaining off the newest port instead would copy that port’s drift.

notes.title: Fixed on the master — the reel’s continuity bug
notes.text: In the owner’s reel the lights she plugs in are not connected to the tree. THE CONNECTION block (one unbroken wire from plug → knot → floor → tree) plus THE TREE IS NOT SWITCHED ON fixed it; the tree must be dark in the frame or the fire has no cause. notes.title: Worked — the camera IS the phone
notes.text: “Held iPhone” written into a POV prompt renders a phone into the bottom of the frame. The opening paragraph declares the camera to BE the phone and bans phone, screen, hand, fingers, thumb, arm, sleeve. No phone appeared in any of the four clips.

notes.title: Failed, then fixed — the camera ran down the hallway (v9 clip g5)
notes.text: g5 said the camera retreats; it walked backwards the whole hall. The owner: “The person filming must make just a few steps back not run the entire hall. In rest is good.” The fix was not a softer adjective: the retreat got an end time (“finished by about 1.6s”), the rest of the clip got a stated camera state (“STANDING STILL … not moving backwards at all”), and the failure itself went into BANNED . A camera move needs a stop time the same way a beat needs a start time.

notes.title: Known and accepted — the fire is late
notes.text: The prompt fuses plug, bulbs, flame, shout and flinch into one instant at 0.8 s; every take still renders plug → flash → fire. Measured: v9 g6 bulbs ≈1.5 s, fire ≈1.8 s; the ports light up by ≈1.7 s and burn by ≈2.0 s. The owner approved all four this way and asked for g6 to be kept as is. Do not change the timing on a port. The written-up fix, untested: move the instant to 0.4 s and delete “flashes on for a split second” — only if the owner asks.
